texts.facts: 2. The Petitioner, apprehending eviction of his Fast Food Stall, has filed this writ petition seeking for a direction to allow him to continue his business in the place, where his Fast Food Stall is operating. The case of the Petitioner was recommended by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Government of India to avail the benefit under PMSVA Nidhi Scheme. The Petitioner made an application on 18th October, 2023 in the prescribed Designation: JUNIOR STENOGRAPHER Location: HIGH COURT OF ORISSA, CUTTACK Date: 01-May-2025 18:44:19 format to issue street vending license in his favour, which is yet to be Sanjay Kumar Das vs State Of Odisha And Others .... Opp. ... on 1 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145779125/ 1 considered. Hence, this writ petition has been filed for the aforesaid relief. Copy of the said application annexed to the writ petition as Annexure-2 does not bear any signature in token of receipt of such application. Although the application is stated to have been filed on 18th October, 2023, immediately thereafter the writ petition has been filed on 15th March, 2025. The Petitioner has no locu standi to be issued with a street vending license.
texts.arguments: 3. Mr. Mohapatra, learned counsel submits that the Petitioner was issued with a Food Safety Certificate under the Provision of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 on 24th December, 2024, which is valid till 11th January, 2030. The Petitioner is running such Fast Food Stall at Nandan Vihar Square, Star City Area, Bhubaneswar. 4. Mr. Panda, learned counsel for Bhubaneswar Municipal Corporation submits that no such application has yet been received by the Town Vending Committee of Bhubaneswar Municipal Corporation (BMC). 5. Considering the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, this Court feels that if the Petitioner intends to get vending certificate under the provisions of the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014 and the Rules framed thereunder, he should make a fresh application in that regard enclosing relevant documents and information.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 3. Mr. Mohapatra, learned counsel submits that the Petitioner was issued with a Food Safety Certificate under the Provision of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 on 24th December, 2024, which is valid till 11th January, 2030. The Petitioner is running such Fast Food Stall at Nandan Vihar Square, Star City Area, Bhubaneswar. 4. Mr. Panda, learned counsel for Bhubaneswar Municipal Corporation submits that no such application has yet been received by the Town Vending Committee of Bhubaneswar Municipal Corporation (BMC). 5. Considering the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, this Court feels that if the Petitioner intends to get vending certificate under the provisions of the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014 and the Rules framed thereunder, he should make a fresh application in that regard enclosing relevant documents and information.
